findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain, so stale or cross-site translations are served
findings.body:
The LRU cache key is built only from `key`, `config.locale` and the backend's `object_id`. With this PR, the value returned for a missing key depends on the fallback chain `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]`. The site's default locale is not part of the key.

In multisite, one process serves sites with different `default_locale` values. A string resolved through site A's default locale gets cached and is then returned to site B, which should have fallen back to its own default.

The same happens on a single site: after an admin changes `default_locale`, cached fallback strings keep the old language until the LRU entry is evicted.

Fix: include the default locale (or the whole fallback chain) in the cache key, or clear the cache when the setting changes.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in ApplicationController, not in jobs or other entry points
findings.body:
`translate` lazily loads only `config.locale`. The fallback locales (site default and :en) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` inside `ApplicationController#set_locale`.

Code that sets `I18n.locale` and translates outside a controller never loads them. That includes Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and controllers or middleware that skip `set_locale`.

In those paths a key missing from the user's locale finds no data in the fallback locales and returns a 'translation missing' string, even though fallbacks are configured.

Fix: load the fallback locales from inside `translate`/`load_locale` instead of relying on the controller hook.

findings.title: SiteSetting is read and a new array allocated on every fallback lookup
findings.body:
`FallbackLocaleList#[]` runs `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`, builds a new array and calls `uniq`/`compact` each time it is invoked. The Fallbacks backend calls it on every uncached translation, i.e. any `I18n.t` call with interpolation or options.

This overrides Hash's memoizing behaviour and puts a SiteSetting lookup plus several allocations on a very hot path.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
